2027-01-10.title: Second Sunday of Denha
2027-01-10.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The ark of the covenant went before them
Israel is saved by the Lord with everlasting salvation
Jesus is worthy of more glory than Moses
Grace and truth came through Jesus Christ
2027-01-10.verse: And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
theo: Denha celebrates the manifestation of the Lord, and today's Gospel puts its heart into one sentence: “And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory.” The Greek verb means that the Word pitched his tent among us. Israel already knew a God who travels with his people. In the Book of Numbers the tribes leave Sinai “with the ark of the covenant of the LORD going before them three days' journey, to seek out a resting place for them”, and the cloud of the Lord is over them by day. Whenever the ark set out, Moses prayed: “Arise, O LORD, let your enemies be scattered.” God did not stay on the mountain; he went ahead of his people on the road.

Isaiah confesses the same mystery from the other side: “Truly, you are a God who hides himself, O God of Israel, the Savior.” The Creator whose hands stretched out the heavens is beyond our sight, and yet he saves: “Israel is saved by the LORD with everlasting salvation.” John answers this longing of every human heart: “No one has ever seen God. It is God the only Son, who is close to the Father's heart, who has made him known.” The hidden God has shown his face in Jesus. That is Denha: the God who hides himself becomes visible in a child of Nazareth, in a man baptised in the Jordan, in the Lord who walks the road with us.

The Letter to the Hebrews compares Moses and Jesus. Moses was faithful in God's house as a servant; “Christ, however, was faithful over God's house as a son, and we are his house if we hold firm the confidence and the pride that belong to hope.” John says the same: “The law indeed was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.” The law was a gift; Christ is the Giver himself. “From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace.” In the Holy Qurbana that fullness is offered to us again: the Word who pitched his tent among us dwells on our altar and in our hearts, and we become his house, his tent among the nations.
conn: The Greek word in John 1:14 (eskēnōsen) recalls the tent of meeting in the wilderness, where the glory of the Lord dwelt in the midst of Israel. Jesus is God's dwelling with his people.
The ark of the covenant held the tablets of the law. It went before Israel as the sign of God's presence. The Fathers saw in it a figure of Christ, and also of Mary, who carried the Word in her womb.
Moses' prayer when the ark set out (Numbers 10:35) is echoed at the start of Psalm 68 and is still said in synagogues when the Torah scroll is taken out for reading.
Isaiah 45 speaks of Cyrus, the Persian king whom God raised up to free the exiles (45:1, 13). God guides history even through those who do not know him.
Hebrews 3:1 is the only place in the New Testament where Jesus himself is called an apostle: the one sent by the Father.
In the Holy Qurbana the Gospel is proclaimed with lights and incense, because in it the Word who dwelt among us speaks to his people today.
altar: The Word who became flesh and lived among us gives himself on the altar under the signs of bread and wine. The tent of meeting has become the Holy Qurbana.
John says that from his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace. At Communion we receive that fullness: Christ himself.

live: Read John 1:1–18 slowly once this week and stop at the verse that touches you.
Before you leave home each morning, pray as Moses did: Arise, O Lord, go before me today.
Spend ten minutes before the Blessed Sacrament, where the Lord hides himself in order to stay near us.
Each night write down one grace you received that day.
fathers: The Word became man so that we might share in the life of God; he took what is ours in order to give us what is his.
Christ as man is the way, Christ as God is the homeland. Walk by the man, and you will come to God.
magis: In his Son the Father has said everything; there will be no other word.
Christ's whole life reveals the Father.
God speaks to us as friends and lives among us.
saints: 14 Jan: St Devasahayam. 15 Jan: Second Friday of Denha, Sts Peter and Paul.
2027-01-10.prayer: O Lord our God, you went before your people in the ark and in the cloud, and in the fullness of time your eternal Word became flesh and pitched his tent among us. Grant that we who have received from his fullness grace upon grace may hold firm our hope, become your living house, and walk with him until we see your glory face to face. To you, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, be glory, now and always and for ever. Amen.

2027-01-10.question: Do I let Christ go before me on the road, or do I walk alone?
kidsaint: The beloved disciple wrote that the Word became flesh and lived among us. Lesson: Jesus came to live close to us, and he wants to live in your heart too.
term: The eternal Son of God took a human nature and became man without ceasing to be God (John 1:14; CCC 461–463).

family.explain: God's Son came to live with us as a real man, Jesus. Through him we receive gift after gift from God.
family.intention: We pray that Jesus may live in our home and walk with us every day.
family.ask: Ask: “What gift from God did you receive today?”

illus: A nurse from Kottayam working in a hospital in Kuwait keeps a small crucifix and a copy of St John's Gospel in her locker. When a colleague asked why, she answered: our God did not stay far away; he came to live where we live. So even here, far from home, I am not alone.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, eternal Word made flesh, you pitched your tent among us. Walk with us as we gather in your name. Amen.
share: Whenever the ark set out, Moses prayed: Arise, O Lord (Numbers 10:35). Do I let God go before me?
Truly, you are a God who hides himself (Isaiah 45:15). Where has God seemed hidden in my life?
From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace (John 1:16). Which graces can I name today?
interc: For the Church, God's house, that she may hold firm her hope.
For migrants and travellers, that they may know God walks with them.
For those who find God hidden, that they may see his face in Jesus.
For our families, that Christ may dwell in our homes.
For our group, that we may receive grace upon grace.
pm.close: Father, your Word became flesh and dwelt among us, full of grace and truth. Make us his faithful house and lead us on the road to your glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the season of Denha keeps one question before us: how has God shown himself to us? Today's Gospel answers in a single line: the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory (John 1:14).

Long before Bethlehem, God was already a travelling God. In the Book of Numbers Israel leaves Sinai with the ark of the covenant going before them to seek out a resting place for them, and the cloud of the Lord over them by day (Numbers 10:33–34). Moses even begs his relative Hobab to come along: come with us, and we will treat you well. And whenever the ark set out, Moses prayed: Arise, O Lord! God did not stay on the mountain; he went ahead of his people.

Yet Isaiah also knows the pain of faith: truly, you are a God who hides himself (Isaiah 45:15). Many of us know that feeling. We pray, and God seems silent. John gives the answer: no one has ever seen God; it is God the only Son, close to the Father's heart, who has made him known (John 1:18). If you want to know what God is like, look at Jesus.

The Letter to the Hebrews tells us that Moses was faithful in God's house as a servant, but Christ is faithful over God's house as a son, and we are his house (Hebrews 3:5–6). John says: the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ (John 1:17). The law showed the way; Jesus is the Way himself.

From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace (John 1:16). Every Holy Qurbana is that fullness given again. The Word who pitched his tent among us comes to dwell in us, and we leave the church as his house, carrying him into our streets and homes.

So this week, before you leave home each morning, pray the prayer of Moses: Arise, O Lord, go before me today. And each night count one grace you received. We are his house; let us let him live in it. Amen.
kids: Children, long ago God's people carried a special golden box called the ark, and it went in front of them on the road to show that God was with them. Then God did something even better: his Son Jesus became a baby and came to live with us!
When you walk to school, say: Jesus, walk in front of me today. He will!
